summary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,652.86 down 0.28% for a second straight session as technology sold off ahead of NVIDIA earnings Wednesday, while the Dow held at 53,417.16 up 0.26% as investors rotated into defensives, with Consumer Staples up 1.70% and Financials up 1.29% leading the session. The 10 year yield eased to 4.70% down 0.72%, helped by Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond buyback program that could exceed 4 billion dollars per operation and may draw on the Treasury General Account, which also lifted gold to 4,684.10 up 0.93%. Bitcoin crossed and held above 79,857.87 up 1.13% as crypto benefited from the same liquidity narrative driving gold, while crude oil dropped to 82.84 down 2.55% as markets continued to shrug off US Iran sanctions. The biggest single stock story was the semiconductor complex, with MU falling 5.83%, IONQ down 8.47%, WDC down 5.24%, and NVDA off 2.91%, all in the final hours before NVIDIA reports Wednesday evening. The US Canada trade war intensified, with Ottawa announcing retaliatory tariffs after talks collapsed and Trump threatening 50 percent levies on Canadian autos, directly pressuring the Canadian side of the book. The week's defining data arrives Wednesday with preliminary GDP, Core PCE, and then Fed Chair Warsh speaks Friday alongside the preliminary benchmark payrolls revision.
